description: GlRaster's textured walk (`#tune 32 1`, roadmap S3.29) is not exact on every probe of the real generic GL: perm_rand 16 values (+3 coverage px), perm_big 12 (+1), const_rand 5, alt_big 1 of 74,418 / 73,803 / 388,800 / 477,802 px stay wrong, and each of them flips with a change of 1-2 float32 ulps of u or v (one needs 10 ulps in a row start 34 rows down; log/roadmap/S3/29_needed.py). Ruled out on these probes (29_texfit.py, 29_notes.md section 2): the gradient anchor (min-y vertex is best; max-y, middle, stream order 0 / 1 / 2 worse), divide vs reciprocal, x87-style double intermediates with any subset of stores, the row step as two adds, repeated pixel steps or precomputed little / big steps, the first-row start from a vertex prestep, an edge-carried walk, the restart at the middle vertex continued or taken from a vertex. The remaining detail of the generic GL's float32 setup (the order of one product or sum) is not determined.
needed: a probe isolating one triangle orientation per scene (fixed vertex order, one attribute ramp) and the flips of 29_flips.py on it

description: A triangle whose texture is GL_NEAREST in both filters takes another interpolation path of the generic GL: s329_cramp_near (constant texture, colour ramp) differs from GlRaster in 141,660 of 477,802 px and s329_uramp_near in 75,964, with the exact plane and with the float32 walk alike (the walk is restricted to textures with a GL_LINEAR filter). The terrain's textures are mag NEAREST / min LINEAR, for which the walk is exact also on magnified (NEAREST-sampled) pixels (s329_cramp_mix / uramp_mix 31 / 22 -> 0), so no recorded terrain pass reaches this path; the probes say nothing about its arithmetic.
needed: the slow-ramp probes of 29_probes.py with an all-NEAREST texture, read with 29_flips.py (the 16.16 untextured stepping of S3.21b is the first candidate)

description: The blend (GL_SRC_ALPHA / GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) of a walked pixel is not determined: on the boundary probe s329_fin_blend (RGBA texture over a flat background, each quad's exact blend on a 5-bit boundary for one dither cell) GlRaster's double blend gives 11,264 wrong channel values of 1,115,136, the best float32 form (src * a + dst * (1 - a) in the 5-bit scale, a = alpha byte / 255.0f, the dither added in float32) 976 (61 of 1,452 boundary cells, each 16 px), every other tested form 1,008 .. 5,792 (log/roadmap/S3/29_blendfit.py). GlRaster keeps the double blend for blended pixels under `#tune 32`.
needed: the order of the blend's products / sums or its alpha conversion: more forms on fin_blend, then a probe with alpha 0 / 255 edges

description: What is left of the terrain residue under the walk is not interpolation: on the seven c7 passes (one-level 173 -> 154) the rest is (a) per-vertex colour (fuzz1_z0: whole tile bands of 414..434 with both signs, margins up to 0.017 5-bit units, the lighting stage U-1308), (b) coverage ownership (32 of the one-level px lie within 0.005 px of a triangle edge; on the terrain-shaped probe s329_iso_cov 51 px and s329_iso_cov_z0 100 px take another triangle than GlRaster's exact-edge rule gives, the real owner's edge passing 2e-6 .. 2.4e-3 px on the far side of the centre, also within the first rows of an edge; fixed-point edge walks at 2^-4 .. 2^-16, float32 edge walks and unsnapped vertices do not reproduce it, 29_covfit.py), (c) blended pixels (U-1967). (b) also gives the iso probes' pixels beyond one level (25 / 13 / 50), which the walk does not touch.
needed: (a) U-1308's float lighting; (b) a coverage probe with single edges at controlled slopes and offsets of 2^-12 .. 2^-8 px from pixel centres

description: The walk's colour attribute for a lit vertex is float32(float32(c) x 31): the generic GL lights in float32 and GlRaster in double (U-1308), so the real vertex colour can differ in its last float bits from float32(c); the probes give the colour through glColor4f (exactly float), where float32(c x 31) and float32(float32(c) x 31) are the same. Not separated on the terrain.
needed: U-1308's float lighting, then the c7 passes with and without the double colour
